A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Rectified Point Flow, with matching authors, core methods, benchmarks, and Appendices A–F. The text, tables, figures, and equations support a complete comparison, including identifying relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original registration and assembly experiments in Section 4, plus rigidity measurements, generative-model comparisons, and qualitative analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds encoder comparisons, cylinder partition tests, FRACTURA evaluation, runtime measurements, and anchor-free experiments.

M1.justification: Appendix B adds an anchor-free variant: the anchor input is centered and randomly rotated, the assembled flow target is recentered, and predictions undergo anchor alignment using ICP. This is a procedural adaptation; the core encoder, DiT architecture, flow-matching objective, and SVD pose recovery remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds synthetic cylinders with horizontal, axial, and random partition scenarios, and zero-shot FRACTURA evaluation covering human and pig bones. It also evaluates prediction without a supplied anchor pose. The original six benchmarks, Objaverse pretraining, and PartNet composition tests remain.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds a ShapeNet-pretrained Point-BERT encoder as a comparator on PartNet-Assembly. Existing benchmark and category-specific comparator sets are retained. GARF's inclusion in the new cylinder and FRACTURA experiments extends an existing comparator to new coverage.

E3.justification: New protocols include anchor-free evaluation after ICP alignment, average and best-of-three prediction reporting, a 6,000-training/600-testing cylinder experiment, zero-shot bone evaluation, and a 1–50 sampling-step runtime study. The rotation-error footnote also expands the stated geodesic reevaluation from GARF to all baselines, although Table 2 values remain unchanged; this does not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of alternative encoder pretraining, transfer across partition schemes and into bone fractures, sampling-step sensitivity, and dependence on known anchor poses. These substantially expand the questions investigated. The original rigidity, RF-versus-DDPM, noise-space, and part-composition analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix B newly specifies three inference seeds per sample for best-of-three anchor-free evaluation, alongside average results. This adds quantitative sampling-budget information, not evidence of additional training runs. Neither version reports confidence intervals, dispersion estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The principal benchmark scores and matched original appendix tables retain their values, but substantial new results appear. For example, FRACTURA zero-shot Part Accuracy is 64.4% for the proposed method versus GARF's 57.7%; PartNet anchor-free accuracy is 45.3% on average and 54.3% best-of-three. These are newly reported comparisons under their stated conditions, not across-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The flow equations, symmetry-group definition, invariance theorem and proof, and Procrustes/Rademacher generalization argument are retained. Appendices E–F contain the same substantive assumptions and derivations despite pagination and citation-number changes.

C1.justification: The unified-framework, symmetry-handling, joint-training, and six-benchmark performance claims remain. Section 2 broadens the furniture-assembly novelty claim by dropping the qualifier 'class-agnostic' from 'first solution.' The Broader Impact paragraph also adds a speed-based claim about accessibility in resource-constrained settings.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly identifies supplied anchor poses as unrealistic and argues for anchor-free evaluation, explaining degradation through anchor misalignment and symmetry ambiguity. It also adds interpretations concerning transferable shape priors, Point-BERT's coarse tokenization and missing contact supervision, and the potential value of medical-domain training. These materially expand applicability qualifications and mechanism explanations.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents largest-volume anchor selection, the TUD-L preprocessing reference, and reuse of the jointly pretrained encoder for TwoByTwo's Single model. It supplies cylinder-generation details, anchor-free processing instructions, Point-BERT tokenization information, and RTX 4090 runtime hardware. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained experiments; code/model access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Imagination Policy, Point-BERT, and ShapeNet references, including discussion of generative point-cloud pose recovery in manipulation. It removes Wang et al.'s Equivariant Flow Matching for Point Cloud Assembly and the associated comparison and exclusion rationale. The furniture-assembly novelty qualification is also broadened, while most positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction rewrites and reorders the three methodological advantages, terminology shifts from self-supervised to overlap-aware pretraining, and Appendix B reorganizes existing evaluations around added studies. The main section structure and most method, conclusion, and theoretical prose remain stable.

P2.justification: V2 adds dedicated tables for partition transfer, FRACTURA, runtime, and two anchor-free comparisons. Table 1 gains a part-definition column, and Table 4 gains dataset grouping and an additional comparison block. Existing appendix tables are reordered, while retained Figures 9 and 10 now share a page. The substantial additions are principally tabular rather than new qualitative figures.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses an important evaluation gap by exposing the advantage of supplied anchor poses and testing an anchor-free variant with its performance costs. Controlled partition-transfer, encoder, medical-domain, and runtime experiments substantially strengthen assessment of the central generalization and practicality claims. These gains outweigh weaknesses in the revision, including broader novelty wording, removal of the concurrent-work discussion, and unexplained reference-score discrepancies such as BreakingBad's fixed-anchor PA of 93.5% in Table 11 versus the retained joint-model 91.1% in Table 2.
